contract: construct() -> an integer k with 1 <= k <= 10^9. The score is the number of powerful integers (p | n implies p^2 | n) strictly between k^2 and (k+1)^2, counted exactly through the unique form a^2 b^3 with b squarefree. Maximize; the optimum is 11 (first at k = 472532614).
notes: For k <= 10^9 the maximum is 11. Erdős's h(n) counts [n^2, (n+1)^2) and so also includes the square n^2; the task counts the open interval as in OEIS A119241. Exact local certificates are not Lean proofs; the Mahler measure and reciprocal sums are reported as floats. Consult the independent oracle and malformed-input tests.

sources.locator: P. Shiu, On the number of square-full integers between successive squares (1980). Crossref record inspected; OEIS A119242 inspected: the least k with exactly 11 powerful numbers strictly between k^2 and (k+1)^2 is 472532614, the least with 12 is 78102676912, and a(n) > 10^11 for n >= 13 (Donovan Johnson), so 11 is the maximum for k <= 10^9. Erdős Problem #942 page inspected (Shiu proved every count occurs with positive density; De Koninck and Luca gave growth rates for large counts). For k <= 10^9 the maximum is 11. Erdős's h(n) counts [n^2, (n+1)^2) and so also includes the square n^2; the task counts the open interval as in OEIS A119241.
